title: How the crypto system turns market data into a signal
subtitle: Three agents read whales, the order book and Reddit mood at once; Llama on Groq weighs them into BUY, SELL or HOLD.

nodes.label: Trader
nodes.detail: Asks for a signal on a pair such as BTC/USDT from the Streamlit dashboard, the REST API or the WebSocket feed.
nodes.tradeoff: The README says the signals are for education, not financial advice.

nodes.label: Signal API
nodes.detail: POST /signal runs the orchestrator; the /ws/signals WebSocket sends a new BTC/USDT signal every 60 seconds.
nodes.tradeoff: /signals/history reads earlier signals back from the database.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.detail: Gathers whale, order book and sentiment results concurrently, fetches the live price from Binance via CCXT, then hands everything to the coordinator.
nodes.tradeoff: A failed agent is replaced by a neutral reading, so one dead source doesn't stop the signal.

nodes.label: Whale tracker
nodes.detail: Pulls unconfirmed transactions over 100 BTC from the Blockchain.com API and scores accumulation versus distribution from -100 to +100.
nodes.tradeoff: A circuit breaker stops calling the API for 60 seconds after 3 failures.

nodes.label: Order book
nodes.detail: Fetches the exchange order book through CCXT and measures bid/ask imbalance, depth and spread.
nodes.tradeoff: It keeps recent snapshots so it can flag likely spoofing.

nodes.label: Sentiment model
nodes.detail: Scores hot posts from r/CryptoCurrency and r/Bitcoin with FinBERT from -1 to +1, and adds the Fear & Greed Index.
nodes.tradeoff: FinBERT loads on first use rather than at startup.

nodes.label: Redis cache
nodes.detail: Each agent checks Redis first. Whale data is kept 60 seconds, order books 30 and sentiment 300.
nodes.tradeoff: If Redis is unavailable, the cache falls back to process memory.

nodes.label: LLM coordinator
nodes.detail: Llama 3.1 70B on Groq gets all three readings plus the whale-versus-retail gap and returns JSON: signal, confidence 0 to 100, and a thesis.
nodes.tradeoff: If the call fails or the JSON is invalid, a rule-based fallback applies the same divergence logic.

nodes.label: Signal store
nodes.detail: Each finished signal, with its price and timestamp, is written to PostgreSQL through asyncpg.
nodes.tradeoff: Without a database it keeps signals in memory instead.

flow.text: Asks for a BTC/USDT signal from the dashboard.
POST /signal hands the symbol to the orchestrator.
Starts the whale, order book and sentiment agents at the same time.
Scores recent large BTC transfers as accumulation or distribution.
FinBERT scores Reddit posts; the Fear & Greed Index adds the crowd's mood.
Weighs whales against retail mood; a gap over 50 points means high confidence.
Saves the signal with its price and timestamp.
Gets BUY, SELL or HOLD with a confidence and a written thesis.

takeaways.text: Agents run concurrently, and a failed one becomes a neutral reading, so a signal still arrives.
The core idea is contrarian: whales buying while retail is fearful reads as bullish, and the reverse as bearish.
Each source is cached on its own clock: order book 30 seconds, whales 60, sentiment 300.
